problem: Chen and Mooney (2011)'s lexicon learning for grounded language acquisition (navigation instructions paired with ambiguous perceptual context) works by intersecting graphs. It only works in batch mode and does not scale to large datasets.
motivation: A semantic lexicon is an important first step for learning to interpret natural language, especially when training data pairs language with ambiguous perceptual context. A fast, online learner makes it possible to use more data, such as data collected from Mechanical Turk, and to test across languages.
key_idea: An online lexicon learning algorithm for ambiguous relational grounded data that is an order of magnitude faster than graph-intersection batch learning and surpasses the state of the art.
insight: Only the abstract was available. It claims that changing the grammar of the formal meaning representation language and adding Mechanical Turk training data further improves results. A Chinese translation of the training data is used to show the approach generalizes across languages. No ablation details are available.
method: Online lexicon learning: an incremental algorithm that replaces the batch graph-intersection lexicon learning of Chen and Mooney (2011).
Meaning representation grammar change: modifies the grammar of the formal meaning representation language to improve results.
Extra data: additional training data collected from Amazon Mechanical Turk.
Multilingual test: evaluation on a Chinese translation of the training data.

setting.backbone: Lexicon learner plus semantic parsing/navigation system (details not in abstract)
setting.training_data: Navigation instruction data (Chen and Mooney 2011 corpus), additional Mechanical Turk data, and a Chinese translation of the data

results: The paper claims the online algorithm is an order of magnitude faster than the batch method and surpasses the state-of-the-art results. Further gains come from a changed meaning representation grammar and extra Mechanical Turk data. No numbers are given in the abstract.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details and numbers are unknown
Evaluated on a single-domain navigation instruction corpus, per the abstract
